summary: Quarterly check-in focused on SLO alignment and runway stability. Customer is seeing intermittent p99 latency spikes on checkout-related calls, wants updated SLOs tied to cost impact, and is evaluating a small Dedicated pool for latency-sensitive traffic. Action items center on benchmark runs, traffic profile sharing, and a revised SLO/pricing proposal.
topics: p99 latency spikes and root-cause hypotheses
Dedicated vs Hosted routing policy for checkout flow
Cost modeling for mixed workload (low-latency + batch embeddings)
transcript:
[00:00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick check — audio ok?
[00:00:06] Alex (Peregrine): Yeah, loud and clear. We have Jordan and Priya on from infra.
[00:00:12] Sofia: Great, today's goal: walk SLO options, surface the p99 behavior you saw, and line up the bench so we can quantify cost/latency tradeoffs. Marcus will lead the technical bit.
[00:00:24] Marcus (Redwood SE): Hi all. Priya, can you give a quick recap of the symptomset so we align on what to measure?
[00:00:32] Priya (Peregrine): Sure — so since launch month we been mostly fine but last two weeks we've had intermittent spikes on our checkout endpoint; p50 is fine, p95 okay, but p99 jumps to 1.6s sometimes 2.2s when concurrency hits around 80–90 requests. It's not consistent, seems correlated with longer prompt sequences and when third-party enrichment calls return slowly.
[00:00:55] Marcus: That's helpful, thanks. Couple immediate Qs: are you sending full context each time or relying on prefix/KV cache?
[00:01:03] Priya: We do a full context send for simplicity — we've not integrated Redwood's prefix caching yet. We were worried about cache invalidation with user-specific context.
[00:01:13] Marcus: Got it. Two levers then — caching and routing to a dedicated low-latency pool for checkout. Both have costs.
[00:01:22] Jordan (CTO): Can you ballpark the incremental cost of a small Dedicated pool? We're trying to compare against rewriting to reduce prompt length which also has engineering time.
[00:01:31] Sofia: We can. We'll include that in the SLO/pricing doc. For rough sense, a dedicated 1–2 GPU pool for heavy tail traffic can be more predictable but shows up as committed capacity with monthly cost. Hosted routing with a model variant can be cheaper but less predictable for p99.
[00:01:46] Alex: Also, we'd like to keep data in our VPC for regulatory reasons — is the Dedicated option the same as Private? I thought Dedicated was still Redwood-hosted.
[00:01:56] Marcus: Good call-out. Dedicated offers isolated GPU pools but runs in Redwood regions; it isn't the same as Private (VPC). If you need customer-managed VPC, that's Redwood Private. Dedicated gives data isolation at rest and strict tenancy but network egress still goes through Redwood infra unless you choose Private.
[00:02:13] Priya: Ok, so Dedicated gives tenancy and capacity guarantees, but not full VPC control. That might be fine for now. We need to check the audit log retention and KMS integration — legal asked.
[00:02:23] Hannah (CSM): We can share the SOC 2 and KMS integration docs — I'll ping them after the call. Also note there's an add-on for longer audit retention if you need.
[00:02:33] Jordan: Good. Back to latency — do you think quantization or model variant selection could materially change p99? We're currently using redwood/gpt-small-1 (example name, actual model varies).
[00:02:45] Marcus: Two pieces — model architecture and serving configuration. Quantization often reduces throughput cost but can slightly change token times; it won't magically fix a tail caused by concurrent KV cache eviction or blocking third-party enrichment. For model choice, a lower-parameter variant with consistent decoding might reduce per-token latency but at some quality cost.
[00:03:04] Priya: The enrichment calls are external and sometimes add 200–600ms. We are considering pre-fetching, but that adds complexity.
[00:03:12] Marcus: For the bench we want to reproduce the composite flow: enrichment + full prompt + model decode. If we can get a traffic histogram and a few representative prompt sets (top 10 prompts by volume), we can replay with similar concurrency and measure p50/p95/p99 and KV cache hit rates.
[00:03:29] Priya: We can do that. We'll share a CSV with token counts distribution and concurrency traces.
[00:03:34] Sofia: Excellent. One thing customers often miss — batching behavior interacts with concurrency. If you have bursty traffic, continuous batching can help cost but might increase tail. We'll include recommended batch/window settings in the doc.
[00:03:46] Alex: We already have a short internal SLA with product — trying to keep checkout under 800ms p99. That's tight.
[00:03:54] Marcus: 800ms p99 is tough at your current traffic patterns without Dedicated and prefix cache. Two paths: 1) invest in prefix/KV cache + shorter prompts so hosted infra meets 800ms most of the time; or 2) route checkout traffic to a small Dedicated pool with pinned GPUs and smaller batching window for strict latency.
[00:04:14] Jordan: What's the measurable delta? Like expected p99 and monthly cost?
[00:04:18] Sofia: We'll put numbers in the proposal. Example: with dedicated 1-GPU pool and optimized routing, you may get p99 ~650–850ms for that flow at expected concurrency; hosted mixed-traffic might be 900–1.6s depending on bursts. But we'll confirm with the bench.
[00:04:34] Priya: Also curious about fallbacks. If dedicated is down, can we auto-failover to hosted without double cost?
[00:04:41] Marcus: Yes — we can configure smart routing with automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in hosted. The objective is graceful degradation, but during failover you might see higher latency and different cost profile. We can set up A/B routing or canary so you don't route all traffic immediately.
[00:04:54] Alex: Ping — curious about cache invalidation approaches for user-specific context. Any patterns you've seen?
[00:05:00] Marcus: Common pattern: prefix cache for static parts of the prompt (product descriptions, business rules) and per-user ephemeral data appended at decode time. That reduces serialized tokens and KV reuse while keeping personalization. There's some engineering work, but it's usually the best cost/latency win.
[00:05:16] Priya: That would require app changes; timeline unknown. Jordan is worried about engineering bandwidth.
[00:05:21] Jordan: Right, we have a rewrite sprint next quarter. If Dedicated can buy us time and meet 800ms, it might be cheaper than a full rewrite now.
[00:05:30] Sofia: That aligns with what other customers choose — Dedicated as a bridge while app changes are scheduled. We'll model the cost of that bridge.
[00:05:37] Hannah: Quick note on observability — Redwood Console can show route-level token breakdown, model-specific latency histograms, and per-token cost. Marcus, can you add screenshots to the proposal so they see the per-route view?
[00:05:48] Marcus: Yep, I'll export the dashboard and include a sample. Also I'll annotate where to look for KV cache hit ratio and continuous batching windows.
[00:05:57] Priya: About security — our security team asked if we can use their Key Management Service for encryption at rest. Is KMS integration available for Dedicated?
[00:06:06] Marcus: KMS/HSM integrations are supported for Private deployments; for Dedicated we offer customer-managed keys in supported regions — there's a short onboarding checklist. I'll include the exact steps and caveats.
[00:06:19] Alex: Great. One more — audit log retention: we need 2 years for compliance. Is that an extra cost?
[00:06:26] Hannah: We have an add-on for extended retention. I'll add pricing to the SLO/pricing doc and include the retention SLAs.
[00:06:33] Jordan: Ok — on contracting: if we go Dedicated for the next quarter as a trial, what's the process to convert to a longer reserve?
[00:06:41] Sofia: We can do a pilot term with month-to-month commitment on a small Dedicated pool and then convert to a 3–12 month reserved contract for discounts. Hannah will draft the amendment.
[00:06:52] Priya: For the bench, can Redwood simulate network variance for enrichment calls so we see composite tail?
[00:06:58] Marcus: Yes, we can add latency injection to the enrichment mock and run the replay. That'll show composite p99.
[00:07:05] Alex: Perfect. Anything else on the technical side?
[00:07:08] Jordan: I'm worried about model drift when we switch variants for latency. How do you monitor quality regressions?
[00:07:15] Marcus: We recommend a small eval set tied to your core checkout prompts — we run automated quality monitoring and set regression alerts. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization/model knobs but quality signals are always tied to your domain test prompts.
[00:07:29] Priya: We'll include a list of 50 critical prompts for eval.
[00:07:33] Sofia: Awesome. Quick recap and owners then next steps.
[00:07:37] Sofia: Action items — Marcus will run the p99 bench (owner Marcus), Priya will send traffic histogram (owner Priya), Sofia/Hannah will draft SLO/pricing and pilot amendment. We agreed target dates on the follow-up email.
[00:07:49] Alex: Sounds good. One tiny thing — competitor question: we are also talking to Anthropic — they quoted lower per-token during the demo but had less mature routing. Any advice?
[00:07:58] Sofia: Price isn't the only angle — look at p99 under realistic traffic, fallback strategies, and operational observability. We'll include a side-by-side in the doc with known tradeoffs.
[00:08:10] Jordan: Ok, thanks everyone.
[00:08:14] Hannah: I'll share SOC 2 and KMS checklist after the call.
[00:08:18] Marcus: I'll propose two bench windows (one for heavy-burst and one steady) and include instructions for the CSV.
[00:08:25] Sofia: Great. We'll follow up with a single-threaded doc and email. Thanks all.
[00:08:30] Alex: Thanks.
[00:08:33] [meeting end — recording stops]
